description: An assistant principal must finalize the school response and re-entry conditions after a student damaged a 3D printer during a technology class, with input from the technology teacher, school counselor, family liaison, and district risk officer.

shared_context.S1: A seventh-grade student damaged a school-owned 3D printer during a technology class, and the printer is currently unavailable for student use.
shared_context.S2: The assistant principal must finalize the disciplinary response, any financial responsibility, and the student's re-entry conditions.
shared_context.S3: The school normally records the response to significant equipment incidents and holds a follow-up meeting with the student and family.
shared_context.S4: Before finalizing an incident response, the assistant principal's routine is to ask the classroom teacher, counselor, family liaison, and district risk officer for relevant information.

PF1.text: Mr. Ibarra directly observed that the student followed the posted operating steps and that a cracked filament spool caused the printer head to jam; the student stopped the machine and reported the damage immediately. He has not yet added this observation to the incident report.

PF2.text: Ms. Novak reviewed the student's active 504 plan, which requires a private disciplinary meeting and a 10-minute regulation break before the student is asked to discuss the incident.

PF3.text: Mr. Hassan confirmed with the family that they need a Spanish interpreter and can attend the follow-up conference only by video call on Thursday at 6:00 p.m.; this confirmation has not yet been entered in the family-contact calendar.

PF4.text: Ms. Greene confirmed with the equipment insurer that the printer damage is fully covered under the school's warranty, so district policy bars charging the student or family any restitution for this incident.

acceptance_conditions: The response must be a restorative conference with no suspension.
The disciplinary meeting must be private and include a 10-minute regulation break before discussion.
The family conference must occur by video call on Thursday at 6:00 p.m.
A Spanish interpreter must be arranged for the family conference.
The restitution amount must be exactly zero dollars.
A restorative-response record must be created.
An interpreter-and-video-conference commitment must be recorded.
A warranty-based no-restitution commitment must be recorded.
The teacher's observation that the damage was accidental must be cited.

decisive_facts.why: The direct observation changes the response from a presumed punitive discipline action to a restorative conference with no suspension and supports the required restorative record.
The active 504 plan changes the disciplinary meeting to a private meeting with an exact 10-minute regulation break and requires the corresponding accommodation commitment.
The family's confirmed constraints change the conference to a Thursday 6:00 p.m. video call, set Spanish as the interpreter language, and require an interpreter-and-video-conference commitment.
The warranty confirmation changes restitution from a possible equipment charge to exactly $0 and requires a documented no-restitution condition.
